verdict_reason: Every quantity is computed from its own definition and I re-derived each: fertility = total_tokens/total_words, compression_ratio = total_tokens/total_chars, token_entropy = -sum p log p over the empirical token-id histogram, vocab_utilization = |distinct ids|/len(tokenizer). I drove the real evaluate() over 13 loadable tokenizers on the shipped config (num_samples=20 of the WikiText-103 validation prefix) and every emitted number matches a hand recomputation. The one substantive implementation choice -- len(tokenizer) rather than tokenizer.vocab_size, so added/special ids cannot push either fraction outside [0,1] -- is correct and is what makes vocab_utilization a genuine fraction (measured 0.0021-0.0186 across the 13, never clipped).
comparable_reason: Measured over 13 tokenizers: the corpus is FIXED, so _meta_total_words = 1400 with std EXACTLY 0 and _meta_total_chars = 7192 with std EXACTLY 0, and therefore pearson(fertility, _meta_compression_ratio) = 1.000000000000 and pearson(fertility, _meta_total_tokens) = 1.000000000000. That claim reproduces to twelve decimals. Two further comparability facts I measured that the fix does not address: (1) vocab_utilization is essentially 1/vocab_size -- pearson +0.9955073334 with 1/vocab_size and -0.905122 with vocab_size, spearman -0.800725 -- so it is an undeclared vocab-size proxy still emitted UNPREFIXED; (2) fertility has almost no resolution: 15 tokenizer requests gave only 7 distinct values, and gpt2 / distilgpt2 / gpt2-medium / opt-125m / phi-2 are BIT-IDENTICAL at 1.215714 (five models, one number), so within a tokenizer family this column carries zero information and functions as a family indicator.
github_reason: Rust et al. 2021 (arXiv:2012.15613) release hgiyt; tokenization_metrics/ computes fertility as the mean number of subword tokens per pre-tokenized word over a reference corpus, which is algebraically the same statistic as BLME's total_tokens/total_words on a whitespace pre-tokenization. I fetched and read it but did not run it head-to-head: it expects a pre-tokenized (word-segmented) corpus and language-specific reference data, so a run would compare different word segmentations rather than different implementations. The definitional check is exact; the numeric head-to-head is not available for the same corpus, hence PARTIAL. There is no released code for the token-entropy or vocab-utilization columns -- those are BLME's own.
paper_reason: Rust et al. report fertility per LANGUAGE for mBERT vs monolingual BERTs on Wikipedia/UD corpora (e.g. mBERT English ~1.6), all on corpora and word segmentations BLME does not use, and Ali et al. 2024 report fertility on their own 5-language mix. Neither publishes a value for any tokenizer BLME can load on the 20-passage WikiText prefix, so no published number is reproducible here. Recording the domain: at num_samples=20 the measurement domain is 1,400 words of ONE WikiText article (the 'Homarus gammarus' lobster article), including WikiText's '@-@' artifacts.
confounds_reason: Direct measurement over 13 tokenizers: vocab_utilization has pearson -0.905122 / spearman -0.800725 with vocab_size and pearson +0.9955 with 1/vocab_size -- it IS vocab_size to within a nearly constant numerator (distinct ids observed varies only 1628-1763 because the corpus is fixed). vocab_size itself is emitted unprefixed but is caught by feature_selection.SIZE_ARCHITECTURE_COLUMNS. fertility/compression_ratio/total_tokens carry pearson +0.5447 with vocab_size. Separately: I confirmed that in the CURRENT analysis pipeline none of this matters, because feature_selection.is_excluded_predictor returns True for ALL NINE emitted keys -- TOKENIZER_PROXY_TERMS matches the substring 'tokenizer' in the flattened column prefix 'geometry_tokenizer_efficiency.', so the whole task contributes zero features. That directly contradicts the module docstring's claim that fertility and vocab_size 'enter BLME's top-25 partial predictors at +0.71 to +0.77'.
defects: Docstring vs pipeline contradiction, unresolved by the fix: the module still claims fertility and vocab_size are top-25 partial predictors at +0.71 to +0.77, but I verified feature_selection.is_excluded_predictor(x) is True for ALL NINE emitted keys (the 'tokenizer' substring in the column prefix triggers TOKENIZER_PROXY_TERMS, and 'tokenizer_efficiency' is also in PERFORMANCE_LIKE_SUBSTRINGS). Either the docstring is describing a pipeline that no longer exists, or the exclusion is wrong. docs/TOP_PREDICTORS.md section 2 has the same problem.

vocab_utilization is an undeclared vocab_size proxy and is emitted UNPREFIXED: pearson +0.9955 with 1/vocab_size, -0.9051 with vocab_size over 13 tokenizers. If the pipeline exclusion above were ever relaxed, this column would enter as vocab_size in disguise. It deserves the same _meta_ treatment as _meta_compression_ratio.

The normalized twin does not normalize: pearson(_meta_normalised_token_entropy, token_entropy) = +0.981478, and its association with vocab_size is WORSE than the raw column's (-0.642661 vs -0.550752). Dividing by log(min(T,V)) is dividing by a near-constant (T ranges only 1628-1763 across the 13 tokenizers, so the divisor varies by 4%).

CONFIG: num_samples=20 makes the measurement domain a single WikiText article. cache.load_default_corpus now documents this and offers diverse=True, but this task does not request it, so the shipped run still measures one lobster article.

Resolution: 7 distinct fertility values over 15 tokenizer requests; five models share the exact value 1.215714. Any regression on this column is regressing on tokenizer FAMILY, not on a graded property.
fix: Not required for GREEN on implementation. To make the reported columns honest: prefix vocab_utilization with _meta_ (it is 1/vocab_size at pearson 0.9955) or replace it with |distinct ids| itself; delete _meta_normalised_token_entropy or renormalise by log of a fixed token budget rather than a near-constant; correct the module docstring and docs/TOP_PREDICTORS.md section 2 to say ONE tokenizer degree of freedom and to state that the analysis pipeline currently excludes this task entirely; and pass diverse=True (or raise num_samples well above 20) so the corpus is not one article.
